title: SDK Upgrade Atelier: codemod runner, example-suite, and automated changelog pipeline for v1->v2
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Ship a lightweight, developer-friendly toolkit ("Upgrade Atelier") that automates the bulk of mechanical work for moving codebases from SDK v1 to v2 while producing a human-reviewable changelog and a runnable example suite across Python/TypeScript/Go.

Motivation: Teams are moving quickly to v2 but repeatedly stumble over three classes of friction: (1) noisy manual churn in large monorepos (find/replace errors), (2) subtle behavioral changes in streaming and retry semantics, and (3) lack of tests/examples to validate runtime ergonomics. Upgrade Atelier should reduce time-to-migration and regression risk by codemodding common patterns, generating a changelog of applied transforms, and running a compatibility test runner that verifies streaming + retry semantics on sample inputs.

Scope: Produce a CLI tool and CI job that: (a) runs language-specific codemods (Python/TS/Go) to apply safe, reversible transformations for the most common v1->v2 API changes, (b) emits a structured but human-readable changelog of all edits suitable for inclusion in release notes, and (c) executes a curated example suite that exercises streaming, retry backoff, and edge cases (timeouts, partial responses) and collects diffs for manual review.
acceptance_criteria: CLI 'upgrade-atelier' can be run in dry-run mode and returns a list of suggested edits with file/line contexts

Codemods for Python, TypeScript, and Go implement >= 90% of mapped patterns for our most common SDK usage documented in telemetry (text generation, chat, embeddings, streaming handlers, retry configs)
Running CLI with --apply writes edits to a git branch, creates a changelog.md summarizing edits and rationales, and opens a draft PR via GitHub API (token provided)
CI job runs example-suite against a smoke staging endpoint and records pass/fail across streaming, retry, and error paths; failures surface as files under 'atelier-report/' in the PR
Generated changelog contains per-file diff snippets and an automated risk score (low/medium/high) based on pattern heuristics
Tooling includes a reversible flag to create a rollback codemod for any applied change
Documentation: a step-by-step migration doc and a short video walkthrough (5–7 minutes) are linked from the PR template
tasks: Design API-to-API mapping doc for v1->v2 (all languages) - owners: Marcus/Aisha
Implement Python codemods using libCST and add unit tests for 120+ patterns
Implement TypeScript codemods using ts-morph and add unit tests
Prototype Go codemod using go/ast and write reversible transforms
Build CLI wrapper (nodejs) that orchestrates language transforms, runs example-suite, and produces changelog.md
Add CI workflow (GitHub Actions) that validates dry-run and apply + example-suite against staging
Create example-suite: 10 canonical examples per language covering streaming, retries, embeddings, tool-calls
Instrument changelog generator to include rationale, risk score, and links to reference docs
Run pilot on 3 internal repos and iterate on heuristics based on observed false-positives
Write docs + short video and add to migration landing page
technical_notes: Codemod approach: favor AST-level rewrites that preserve formatting where possible (libCST for Python, ts-morph for TS, go/ast+printer for Go)
Mapping examples: v1 client.createCompletion(...) -> v2 client.text.generate(...); streaming handler signatures change from on_chunk(chunk) to async for await chunk in stream
Retry mapping: convert legacy retry decorators/options to new RetryPolicy object; codemod will add imports + default policy if absent
Streaming semantics risk: v2 introduces chunk typing (delta vs final); examples need to assert on event types rather than raw strings to avoid flakiness
Changelog generation: include a per-edit UUID, source snippet, transformed snippet, and a one-line rationale (automated) + suggested reviewer (heuristic based on file path)
Rollback: 'atelier rollback --pr 123' will apply reversed edits recorded in the changelog and post a comment on the PR
Performance: codemod run time must be under 30s per 500 files for CI feasibility; use file globs + parallel workers
